   2→
   3→**Status at handoff: 2026-09-23.** Suite 312 tests. **Every failure is in

   7→A second cross-family review (glm-5.3) of fix round one found these. Every item was

   9→for the rules round one established; they still apply.
  10→
  11→## The five items
  12→
  13→### S1 — party_view: only a decision's message may vary
  14→
  15→`app/server.py::party_view` fails closed only for `decided` and `needs_info`. A stale or
  16→planted `human_review` case file relays its own message, e.g. "The AI agent judge will follow
  17→up". **Fix:** every non-decision status shows its **canonical constant**, never the file's
  18→text: `passed_to_support` → `HUMAN_REVIEW_MESSAGE`, `needs_info` → `NEEDS_INFO_MESSAGE`,
  19→`under_review` → `UNDER_REVIEW_MESSAGE` (already). Only `decided` carries the file's message,
  20→and it keeps the banned-word check. Questions keep their check.
  21→
  22→### S2 — the banned-word filter misses word forms and ID variants
  23→
  24→`is_party_safe` passes "models", "judges", "withhold", "judgement", "confident", "advocacy",
  25→lowercase `rd-1`, `Esc-4` and 4-digit IDs. **Fix:** broaden `PARTY_UNSAFE_PATTERN` to stems
  26→(`ai`, `agents?`, `advocat\w*`, `judg\w*`, `confiden\w*`, `withh[eo]ld\w*`, `escalat\w*`,
  27→`models?`) and make the rule-ID pattern case-insensitive with up to 4 digits. Checked before
  28→writing this: no non-ESC rule title, no intake template question and none of the three
  29→canonical messages trips the broader pattern. The test pins that.
  30→
  31→### S3 — near-duplicate questions
  32→
  33→The gate emits a template for a blank field even when a safe model question already asks about
  34→it, and exact-string dedup lets "Where were you?" and "where were you" both through. **Fix,
  35→two parts:**
  36→1. Templates are a **fallback**: collect the safe model questions first. Only if none survive,
  37→   emit template questions for blank fields (at most 3, one per field).
  38→2. Dedup on a **normalised** form: lowercase, drop punctuation, collapse whitespace. Keep the
  39→   first original wording.
  40→
  41→### S4 — a failed bookkeeping write bricks the run
  42→
  43→In `_answer_run`, `claim_path.write_text(...)` (the `answered.json` record) sits outside the
  44→failure handler. If it fails after the round-two run succeeded, the handler returns 500 and
  45→the claim stays, so every retry gets 409. **But releasing the claim is wrong too**: the round-two
  46→run already exists, so a retry would rule twice (the R4 defect by another route).
  47→
  48→**Fix:** move the write into a module-level function `_write_answered_record(claim_path,
  49→new_run_id, cleaned)` (the test patches this name). Call it in a `try`; on `OSError`, log to
  50→stderr and **still return the 200 party view**. The claim file already exists (empty), so the
  51→run stays answered.
  52→
  53→### S5 — escalation rules must never appear in a Basis line
  54→
  55→`ESC-4`'s title "Amount above the autonomous cap" passes the word filter, so a real Judge citing
  56→it would show the cap mechanism to a party. **Fix:** in `_cited_rule_titles`, skip every rule
  57→whose ID starts with `ESC-`, **by prefix**, before any word check. A ruling citing only ESC rules
  58→gets no Basis line.
  59→

  61→
  62→Same as round one: no changes to `data/`, `docs/policy.md`, `tools/`, gates, threshold or cap,
  63→and no test edits unless a test has a genuine bug (say so). The 35 corpus runs keep outcome,
  64→action and amount; `party_message` wording may change only where S5 applies (the mock cites
  65→GEN-1/GEN-2, so it should not change at all).

  70→S2, S3, S4 and S5: revert, show RED, restore. Finish with a summary of what changed and what

  11→2026-09-23), not a design choice left open.
  12→
  13→## The standing rules this round serves
  14→
  15→- **Gates live in code, not in prompts.** Nothing a model writes reaches a party unless code
  16→  built it or code checked it.
  17→- **A type check is not a shape check.** `typeof x === "object"` admits arrays and `{}`. R6 is
  18→  this exact defect class, again; pin the whole family of wrong shapes.
  19→- **A fix is not done until a test fails when the fix is reverted.**
  20→
  21→## The ten items
  22→
  23→### R1 — MAJOR — the decision message relays the Judge's explanation (the operator ruling A)
  24→
  25→`app/schemas.py::party_message_for_ruling` appends `ruling.explanation` verbatim. The mock's
  26→explanation names "the Judge" and "advocate cases" on every decided run; a real model's can
  27→carry its confidence (reproduced: a party saw `0.91`). Pre-dates session six (09-21).
  28→
  29→**Fix, as ruled:** the party message is **built in code** from structured fields only:
  30→- the action and, for refund/compensation, the amount;
  31→- the **plain titles** of the cited rules, e.g. `Basis: When a deviation is material.`
  32→- **no rule IDs, no explanation.** Cited rules whose title would leak (the ESC-* family:
  33→  "Low confidence", "escalation") are skipped. Filter titles through the same banned-word set
  34→  the tests use; no more than 3 titles.
  35→
  36→Add `PolicySet.rule_title(rule_id)` to `app/policy.py`: the heading text after the em dash,
  37→provenance tag `[...]` stripped, ID stripped. Change the signature to
  38→`party_message_for_ruling(ruling, policy=None)`; with no policy the message is action + amount
  39→alone. Pass the policy through at `app/agents/judge.py:209`. **The Judge's explanation stays on
  40→`resolution.ruling.explanation` for the operator console, unchanged.**
  41→
  42→`party_view` (app/server.py) is the second line: for `decided` and `needs_info`, if the message
  43→(or any question) matches the banned-word set, fail closed to the neutral under-review view.
  44→Test: `test_party_view_fails_closed_on_a_leaky_planted_message`.
  45→
  46→### R2 — MAJOR — follow-up questions reach the party as raw model text
  47→
  48→`app/pipeline.py::_questions_for_party` passes advocate output straight through. **Fix:** a
  49→code gate in the pipeline, before the questions are stored. Any question matching the banned
  50→words or a rule-ID pattern (`[A-Z]{2,5}-\d{1,3}`) is **replaced by a template question** for a
  51→blank intake field: `We didn't get an answer to "<form label>". Could you tell us?` Pick blank
  52→fields not already covered; if none is left, drop the question. No duplicates, still at most 3.
  53→If nothing survives, the run does **not** stop (no empty needs_info).
  54→
  55→The template needs the form labels in Python. **Make one owner:** an `INTAKE_QUESTIONS` table in
  56→`app/schemas.py` (`category -> ((key, label), ...)`), labels exactly as `ui/party/party.js`
  57→shows them today. Derive `app/server.py::QUESTIONNAIRES` from it. The test reads party.js and
  58→asserts the two agree.

  62→A `no_show_charge` filing on a route trip → `EvidenceInputError` → **500**. Reachable from the
  63→page: pick "Something else", pick a route trip, switch the category card without pressing
  64→Continue. Reverse direction (route filing on a no-show trip) → a "route distance" built from the
  65→driver's waiting-around GPS (R5, contained by ESC-2 but false evidence).

  68→**400** `this trip does not match the category you picked`, and **no run directory created**.
  69→Out-of-scope categories still accept any trip. **Page side:** changing the category card must
  70→reset the trip choice and hide the later steps.

  74→TOCTOU between the `answered.json` check and the write, on a `ThreadingHTTPServer`. Reproduced:

  81→`ui/app.js:224`, `if (item && typeof item === "object")`. **Fix:** require a non-array object

 284→def _questions_for_party(
 285→    dispute: Dispute, rider_case: AdvocateCase, driver_case: AdvocateCase
 286→) -> List[str]:
 287→    """The follow-up questions to send the filing party, or [] when none.
 288→
 289→    The filing party's own advocate's questions go first, then the other advocate's.
 290→    This is a code gate, not a pass-through (R2): a question that would leak the
 291→    internal vocabulary or carries a rule ID is REPLACED by a template question for a
 292→    blank intake field, named by its form label. No blank field left to name -> the
 293→    question is dropped. Duplicates are removed and the list is capped at 3; if nothing
 294→    survives, the run does not stop (an empty needs_info is worse than none).
 295→    """
 296→    if dispute.filed_by == "rider":
 297→        collected = list(rider_case.follow_up_questions) + list(driver_case.follow_up_questions)
 298→    else:
 299→        collected = list(driver_case.follow_up_questions) + list(rider_case.follow_up_questions)
 300→
 301→    # Blank intake fields the template can name, in form order. Only fields this
 302→    # category's form actually asks about get a replacement — the template quotes the
 303→    # field's label, and the label table is the one owner of those words.
 304→    blank_keys = [
 305→        key
 306→        for key, _label in INTAKE_QUESTIONS.get(dispute.category, ())
 307→        if isinstance(dispute.intake.get(key), str) and not dispute.intake[key].strip()
 308→    ]
 309→    used_blank_keys: set = set()
 310→
 311→    gated: List[str] = []
 312→    for question in collected:
 313→        if len(gated) >= 3:
 314→            break
 315→        text = (question or "").strip()
 316→        if not text:
 317→            continue
 318→        if not is_party_safe(text):
 319→            replacement = None
 320→            for key in blank_keys:
 321→                if key not in used_blank_keys:
 322→                    used_blank_keys.add(key)
 323→                    replacement = blank_field_question(dict(INTAKE_QUESTIONS[dispute.category])[key])
 324→                    break
 325→            if replacement is None:
 326→                continue
 327→            text = replacement
 328→        if text not in gated:
 329→            gated.append(text)
 330→    return gated[:3]

Round two complete: 5 commits, full suite **312 tests OK**, working tree clean.

## What changed

- **S1 — `app/server.py::party_view`** (`3e0ae3b`): every non-decision status now shows its canonical constant — `passed_to_support` → `HUMAN_REVIEW_MESSAGE`, `needs_info` → `NEEDS_INFO_MESSAGE`, `under_review` → `UNDER_REVIEW_MESSAGE`. - **S5 — `app/schemas.py::_cited_rule_titles`** (`61e0ae6`): rules whose ID starts with `ESC-` are skipped by prefix before any word check. A ruling citing only ESC rules gets no Basis line.
- **S2 — `app/schemas.py` patterns** (`39f81d1`): `PARTY_UNSAFE_PATTERN` is stem-shaped (`ai`, `agents?`, `advoca\w*`, `judg\w*`, `confiden\w*`, `withh[eo]ld\w*`, `escalat\w*`, `models?`); the rule-ID pattern is case-insensitive with up to 4 digits. One deviation from the brief's sketch: `advoca\w*` instead of `advocat\w*` — "advocacy" has no 't', and the S2 acceptance list requires it caught; the test pins it.
- **S3 — `app/pipeline.py::_questions_for_party`** (`08ca411`): safe model questions are collected first; template questions for blank fields are emitted only when **no** safe question survives (one per field, form order, max 3). Dedup keys on a normalised form (lowercase, punctuation dropped, whitespace collapsed), keeping the first wording.
- **S4 — `app/server.py`** (`e1e70db`): the `answered.json` write moved into module-level `_write_answered_record(claim_path, new_run_id, cleaned)`; on `OSError` it logs to stderr and the handler still returns the 200 party view. - **T1 — `app/schemas.py`** (`91c45bb`): the rule-ID pattern no longer matches any 2-5-letter token — it matches only the prefixes `docs/policy.md` actually uses (`GEN|EV|RD|NS|ESC`), case-insensitive, up to 4 digits, from a new named constant `PARTY_RULE_ID_PREFIXES` (the one owner, commented as such). I."; "plan A. I walked" still passes since there's no dot after the I).

- **T4 — `app/server.py::party_view`** (`eacdabe`): the non-blank-message requirement now applies to `decided` only. Since S1 a non-decision status never displays the file's text, so the old blanket check just discarded a needs-info file's safe questions over a string nobody sees.
